public_job_wage.law: Texas Government Code chapter 2258 (state prevailing wage law). It covers public works of the state and of political subdivisions (cities, counties, school districts), so a City of Houston building or a public school job is covered whether or not federal money is involved. The federal Davis-Bacon Act applies separately to federally funded or assisted contracts over $2,000.
public_job_wage.who_sets_rate: The public body awarding the contract (city council, school board, county), by its own wage survey or by adopting the U.S. Department of Labor's Davis-Bacon rates. Rates therefore differ between owners in the same county.
public_job_wage.state_threshold_note: Chapter 2258 has no dollar threshold; the whole chapter was read. Its limits are: it does not apply to maintenance work (2258.021(b)), and a contractor is not in violation if the public body did not determine the rates and put them in the contract (2258.023(c)).
public_job_wage.penalty: $60 per worker per calendar day underpaid, paid to the public body (2258.023(b)).

access_differences.state_requirement: At least one mirror must be accessible, and accessible mirrors must be placed consistently with the other mirrors in the same room.
access_differences.state_quote: 213.3.5 Mirrors. Where mirrors are provided, at least one shall comply with 603.3. Accessible mirrors shall be provided at locations that are consistent with the location of other mirrors in the same room.

access_differences.point: Who decides when full compliance in an alteration is not feasible
access_differences.state_requirement: In Texas the decision that compliance is technically infeasible is made by TDLR through its variance procedure, not by the owner or designer alone.
access_differences.state_quote: For purposes of ensuring compliance with Texas Government Code, Chapter 469, all determinations of technical infeasibility and maximum extent feasible are made by the Department in accordance with the variance procedures contained in Chapter 68, Texas Administrative Code.
access_differences.federal_quote: In alterations, where compliance with applicable requirements is technically infeasible, the alteration shall comply with the requirements to the maximum extent feasible.
access_differences.note: Relevant when an existing restroom cannot fit a 60-inch wheelchair stall. Both quotes checked against the PDF text.

access_differences.state_quote: If your project's total estimated cost is less than $50,000.00, you are not required to submit the project to the Department for registration and review, however, the project is still required to comply with TAS.

access_summary.finding: The 2012 Texas Accessibility Standards (effective March 15, 2012) use the 2010 ADA Standards' own text and section numbers. A word-level comparison of the two PDFs found no difference in section 213 (apart from the mirror sentence), 216 (signs), 404 (doors), 603 (toilet rooms), 604 (water closets and toilet compartments, including 604.8.1 wheelchair stalls, 604.8.2 ambulatory stalls, doors, toe clearance and 604.9 children's stalls), 605, 606, 609 (grab bars) or 703 (signs). Texas does not go further than the federal standard on stall size, doors, toe clearance, grab bars, restroom door signs or children's stalls. It does not use ICC A117.1.
access_summary.same_in_both_quote: 213.3.1 Toilet Compartments. Where toilet compartments are provided, at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1. In addition to the compartment required to comply with 604.8.1, at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures.
access_summary.method: pdftotext on both PDFs, running page headers stripped, whitespace/hyphen/fraction glyphs normalised, then difflib comparison section by section. Figures (drawings) were not compared.
access_summary.other_texas_wording: TAS 202.4 adds Texas text on path-of-travel work (safe harbor for elements built to the April 1, 1994 TAS; a tenant's alterations in its own space do not trigger path-of-travel work in the landlord's areas). These mirror the U.S. Department of Justice regulations rather than go beyond them.
access_summary.other_texas_quote: those alterations by the tenant in areas that only the tenant occupies do not trigger a path of travel obligation upon the landlord with respect to areas of the facility under the landlord's authority, if those areas are not otherwise being altered
access_summary.city_layer: Houston's building code separately cites ICC A117.1 for multi-user all-gender rooms (see restroom_rules), and the city sends accessibility questions to TDLR.
access_summary.confidence_note: Both standards read in full text from the official PDFs. TDLR's technical memoranda page returned 404 (https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/ab/abtechmemos.htm), so any memo that interprets a stall rule was not checked.

single_user.summary: Under the 2021 International Building Code as adopted by Houston (section 2902.1.2, not amended by the city), single-user toilet rooms and family or assisted-use toilet rooms must be identified as available to all persons regardless of sex, and they count toward the required fixture total. They do not have to be designated by sex (2902.2 exception 5). No Texas statute requires a private owner to make single-user restrooms all-gender; no separate City of Houston ordinance on the subject was found.
single_user.quote: Single-user toilet facility and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use either by all persons regardless of their sex.
single_user.quote_note: Copied from the City of Houston's '2015 Houston IBC Amendments / 2021 International Building Code' comparison PDF, whose text layer keeps struck-out words: the words 'facility' and 'either' are deletions in the 2021 text, which reads '...shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex.' Check against the printed 2021 IBC before quoting.
single_user.second_quote: 5. Separate facilities shall not be required to be designated by sex where single-user toilet rooms are provided in accordance with Section 2902.1.2.
single_user.privacy_quote: Exception: Visual screening shall not be required for single-occupant toilet rooms with a lockable door.
single_user.state_law_note: Texas Government Code 3002.052(a)(2) says the 2025 law on public buildings does not stop a public body from 'establishing a single-occupancy private space, family restroom, or changing room'; 3002.001(9)(A) defines the term as 'a single toilet restroom with a locking door that is designed or designated as unisex or for use based on sex'.

multi_user_all_gender.summary: The 2021 IBC as adopted by Houston allows a multi-user room designed for all genders in place of separate men's and women's rooms. Conditions in the code text: fixture count worked out on 100% of the occupant load; each fixture type meets ICC A117.1; every urinal in a stall (or, under 2902.2 exception 6, in a visually separated area); water closet privacy 'in accordance with Section 405.3.4 of the International Plumbing Code'. The general rule (2903.1.4) is that each water closet has its own compartment with walls or partitions and a door 'to ensure privacy'. The code text read does not require full-height partitions, gap-free doors or occupancy indicators by name; locks are mentioned only for single-occupant rooms.
multi_user_all_gender.quote: 6. Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by both sexes and privacy for water closets are installed in accordance with Section 405.3.4 of the International Plumbing Code. Urinals shall be located in an area visually separated from the remainder of the facility or each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall.
multi_user_all_gender.fixture_count_quote: 2. Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1 and each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall.
multi_user_all_gender.compartment_quote: [P] 2903.1.4 Water closet compartment. Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy.
multi_user_all_gender.base_rule_quote: [P] 2902.2 Separate facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex.
limits: Not available in buildings owned, operated or controlled by a Texas political subdivision or state agency: Government Code 3002.051 requires every multiple-occupancy restroom there to be designated for one sex (see restricting_law).

Houston enforces the 2021 Uniform Plumbing Code, not the International Plumbing Code that exception 6 points to. UPC section 422.2 (the plumbing code's own separate-facilities rule) is not amended by Houston and was not read; ask plumbing plan review which privacy standard it applies to an all-gender multi-user room.
multi_user_all_gender.accessible_stall_note: Advisory text printed in both TAS and the ADA Standards: 'Full-height partitions and door assemblies can comprise toilet compartments where the minimum required spaces are provided within the compartment.' (Advisory 213.3.1)

restricting_law.name: Texas Government Code chapter 3002 (Senate Bill 8, 89th Legislature, 2nd Called Session, 2025; short title 'Texas Women's Privacy Act')
restricting_law.applies_to: Buildings owned, operated or controlled by a political subdivision (county, city, special district, school district, open-enrollment charter school, junior college district) or a state agency (including public universities). It places no duty on private building owners.
restricting_law.quote: A political subdivision or state agency shall designate each multiple-occupancy private space in a building the political subdivision or state agency owns, operates, or controls for use only by individuals of one sex.
restricting_law.second_quote: A political subdivision or state agency shall take every reasonable step to ensure an individual whose sex is opposite to the sex designated for a multiple-occupancy private space under Subsection (a) does not enter the private space.
restricting_law.definition_quote: "Multiple-occupancy private space" means a facility designed or designated for simultaneous use by more than one individual and in which an individual may be in a state of undress in the presence of another individual, regardless of whether the facility provides curtains or partial walls for privacy. The term includes a restroom, locker room, changing room, or shower room.
restricting_law.sex_definition_quote: "Sex" means an individual's biological sex, either male or female.
restricting_law.exceptions_quote: a child who is: (A) nine years of age or younger entering a multiple-occupancy private space designated for the exclusive use of individuals of the sex opposite to the child's sex; and (B) accompanied by an individual caring for the child
restricting_law.other_exceptions: Entry for custodial, maintenance or inspection, medical or emergency, assistance, and law enforcement purposes (3002.053(1)).
restricting_law.penalty_quote: (1) $25,000 for the first violation; and (2) $125,000 for the second or a subsequent violation.
restricting_law.penalty_note: Civil penalty on the political subdivision or state agency; each day of a continuing violation is a separate violation (3002.101). Complaints go to the attorney general after written notice and three business days to cure (3002.102).

shipped_without_installation.summary: Partitions are taxable goods. An out-of-state seller with more than $500,000 of Texas revenue in the preceding twelve calendar months must hold a Texas permit and collect state and local use tax. Such a remote seller may collect the actual local rate at the delivery address (2% in Houston, 8.25% total) or elect the single local use tax rate (currently 1.75%, 8.00% total). If the seller does not charge Texas tax, the buyer owes use tax to the Comptroller.

The current single local use tax rate is 1.75 percent
facts.note: Described on the page as 'an alternative local tax rate' used 'instead of collecting and remitting the total local tax in effect at the destination address', 'published in the Texas Register by Jan. 1 of each year'. Not available to marketplace providers.

facts.quote: A Texas purchaser owes state and local use tax if they buy taxable goods and services from a seller who does not charge Texas sales tax.
A nonpermitted Texas purchaser that does not have a Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit must report and pay any use tax owed to the Comptroller's office on Form 01-156, Texas Use Tax Return

"sales price" or "receipts" means the total amount for which a taxable item is sold, leased, or rented, valued in money, without a deduction for the cost of: ... (3) the transportation or installation of tangible personal property
facts.note: Tax Code 151.007(a): freight charged by the seller is part of the taxable price.

installation_labor_commercial_remodel.summary: In Texas, labor to repair, remodel or restore nonresidential real property is itself a taxable service. Replacing or upgrading partitions in an existing commercial restroom is taxed on the whole charge, materials and labor, even when labor is billed separately. Labor is not taxed on new construction (new buildings, completing unfinished structures, initial finish-out) or on residential property.

facts.quote: the total amount charged for remodeling, repairing, or restoring nonresidential real property is taxable.
facts.note: Texas Comptroller Publication 94-116, 'Real Property Repair and Remodeling' (revision date shown: 03/2007; still published).

facts.quote: When you do any of the following types of jobs on nonresidential real property, the job is taxable: rebuilding real property; upgrading any part of an existing structure; replacing any part of an existing structure, except for minor replacement of parts during maintenance of the real property
you should collect state sales tax plus any local tax on your total charge for the job.

"Real property repair and remodeling" means the repair, restoration, remodeling, or modification of an improvement to real property other than: (1) a structure or separate part of a structure used as a residence
facts.note: Tax Code 151.0047(a); 151.0101(a)(13) lists 'real property repair and remodeling' among taxable services.

furnish_and_install_contract.summary: Depends on the job. Existing nonresidential building (remodel or replacement): the contractor collects tax from the customer on the total contract price and may buy the partitions tax-free with a resale certificate. New construction: under a lump-sum contract the contractor pays tax on the materials when buying them and charges the customer no tax; under a separated contract the contractor buys materials on a resale certificate and collects tax on the materials charge only; construction labor is not taxed. A single contract that mixes new square footage and remodeling is presumed fully taxable when the remodeling part is more than 5% of the price.

facts.quote: Under a lump-sum contract, you pay tax on all your supplies, materials, equipment, and taxable services when you buy them. You don't charge your customer tax.
Under a separated contract, you give your suppliers resale certificates instead of paying tax on materials you incorporate into the customer's real property
The construction labor is not taxable.

If you have a contract to add new square footage and to remodel existing footage in nonresidential realty for a single charge and the portion relating to the remodeling is more than five percent of the total charge, the total charge is presumed to be taxable.
You may give your suppliers resale certificates instead of paying tax on materials that will be incorporated into the customer's real property.
facts.note: From the nonresidential repair and remodeling part: the remodeler buys materials for resale and taxes the whole job.

facts.quote: A contractor is the consumer of tangible personal property furnished by him and incorporated into the property of his customer if the contract between the contractor and his customer contains a lump-sum price covering both the performance of the service and the furnishing of the necessary incidental material.
